fields.title: Family Food Values
fields.label: Family Food Values
fields.subtitle: Primary food values that guide meal preparation decisions in the household
fields.caption: Convenience-first households dominate (102/233, 44%), with health-first (72/233, 31%) and taste-first (48/233, 21%) trailing — appliance messaging should prioritize time-saving over health claims for broadest relevance.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant bar signals the most common meal-prep priority this audience balances against other values.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from how the respondent described their family's meal priorities in the transcript.

legend.label: Convenience First
legend.description: Prioritizes quick/easy meal prep over other values — likely to value appliances that save time.

legend.label: Health First
legend.description: Chooses ingredients and prep methods perceived as healthier, even if less convenient.

legend.label: Taste First
legend.description: Prefers traditional flavors and textures, even if preparation is more labor-intensive.

legend.label: Mixed
legend.description: No single dominant value — balances multiple priorities situationally.

fields.title: Time Pressure Type
fields.label: Time Pressure Type
fields.subtitle: Primary time constraints shaping daily meal preparation routines
fields.caption: Morning rush dominates (156/233, 67%) — appliances that excel at quick breakfast prep (chutneys, smoothies) will resonate more than those optimized for elaborate meals.
fields.how_to_read: The tallest bar shows the most acute time pressure point this audience needs appliances to solve.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from descriptions of daily routines and pain points around meal timing.

legend.label: Morning Rush
legend.description: Most time pressure occurs at breakfast — needs appliances that prep quickly with minimal cleanup.

legend.label: Working Woman Schedule
legend.description: Juggles job demands with meal prep — values appliances that can multitask or operate unattended.

legend.label: None
legend.description: Reports no particular time pressure — may prioritize appliance features unrelated to speed.

legend.label: Business Volume
legend.description: Prepares food in large quantities for commercial purposes — needs heavy-duty capacity.

legend.label: Working Professional Schedule
legend.description: Irregular hours make meal timing unpredictable — values appliances with quick on-demand use.

fields.title: Regional Food Culture
fields.label: Regional Food Culture
fields.subtitle: Dominant regional cuisine styles influencing appliance usage patterns
fields.caption: South Indian cuisine dominates (114/233, 49%) — appliances optimized for wet grinding (idli/dosa batter) will see heavier use than dry choppers in this sample.
fields.how_to_read: The tallest bar indicates the most common regional cuisine driving appliance feature needs.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from descriptions of staple dishes and preparation methods.

legend.label: South Indian
legend.description: Regularly prepares rice-based dishes, chutneys, and wet batters requiring fine grinding.

legend.label: Mixed
legend.description: Cooks diverse regional cuisines without a single dominant style.

legend.label: North Indian
legend.description: Focuses on wheat-based dishes, dry masalas, and occasional wet grinding.

legend.label: East India
legend.description: Prepares fish-based dishes and fermented foods with specialized prep needs.

legend.label: Western India
legend.description: Emphasizes quick snacks and fried items requiring rapid batch processing.

legend.label: West Indian
legend.description: Outlier in sample — likely Caribbean-influenced cuisine with distinct appliance needs.

fields.title: Event Cooking Frequency
fields.label: Event Cooking Frequency
fields.subtitle: Whether the respondent regularly prepares food for large gatherings
fields.caption: Only 19/233 (8%) regularly cook for events — most appliance usage is for daily household meals, not occasional large batches.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'False' bar signals most usage is for routine meal prep, not occasional capacity-heavy events.
fields.calc_note: Directly reported by the respondent when describing their cooking habits.

legend.label: False
legend.description: Primarily cooks for immediate household, not large gatherings.

legend.label: True
legend.description: Regularly prepares food for events or large groups beyond the household.

fields.title: Traditional vs Modern Lean
fields.label: Traditional vs Modern Lean
fields.subtitle: Whether meal preparation skews toward traditional methods or modern conveniences
fields.caption: Overwhelmingly mixed (219/233, 94%) — this audience selectively adopts modern appliances while retaining traditional techniques, rejecting a binary choice.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'mixed' bar signals pragmatic blending of old and new methods rather than ideological purity.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from how the respondent described their balance of traditional and modern cooking approaches.

legend.label: Mixed
legend.description: Uses modern appliances for some tasks while retaining traditional methods for others.

legend.label: Modern Lean
legend.description: Prefers full modernization of kitchen tools with minimal retention of traditional techniques.

fields.title: Generational Knowledge Transfer
fields.label: Generational Knowledge Transfer
fields.subtitle: Whether cooking knowledge is actively passed between generations
fields.caption: Rare (6/233, 3%) — appliance use is largely self-taught rather than handed down, creating openings for beginner-friendly onboarding.
fields.how_to_read: A near-unanimous 'False' indicates most users aren't inheriting appliance skills from elders.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from descriptions of how cooking/appliance skills were acquired.

legend.label: False
legend.description: Learned appliance use independently, not through intergenerational teaching.

legend.label: True
legend.description: Received explicit instruction on appliance use from older family members.

fields.title: Social Proof Reliance
fields.label: Social Proof Reliance
fields.subtitle: Degree to which appliance choices are influenced by others' opinions
fields.caption: Medium reliance dominates (136/232, 59%) — testimonials and visible peer usage matter, but aren't absolute purchase drivers.
fields.how_to_read: A central tendency toward 'medium' signals balanced evaluation between personal needs and social validation.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from how the respondent described the role of peer/family opinions in appliance choices.

legend.label: Medium
legend.description: Considers others' experiences but ultimately decides based on personal needs.

legend.label: High
legend.description: Heavily influenced by what peers/family use or recommend.

legend.label: Low
legend.description: Makes appliance choices independently with minimal social input.

fields.title: Purchase Decision Maker
fields.label: Purchase Decision Maker
fields.subtitle: Primary decision authority for appliance purchases
fields.caption: Self-driven decisions dominate (213/231, 92%) — marketing should target primary cooks directly, not through husbands or family committees.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'self' bar signals women are empowered to choose appliances without requiring male approval.
fields.calc_note: Directly reported by the respondent when describing purchase processes.

legend.label: Self
legend.description: Primary cook makes appliance decisions independently.

legend.label: Joint
legend.description: Appliance choices are made collaboratively with spouse/family.

legend.label: Husband
legend.description: Male head of household has final say on appliance purchases.

fields.title: Household Type
fields.label: Household Type
fields.subtitle: Family structure shaping appliance usage patterns
fields.caption: Nuclear households prevail (144/231, 62%) — appliances are serving smaller, immediate families more than extended kin networks.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'nuclear' bar signals usage is concentrated among parents and children, not shared across generations.
fields.calc_note: Directly reported by the respondent when describing their living situation.

legend.label: Nuclear
legend.description: Parents and children living independently of extended family.

legend.label: Joint
legend.description: Multiple generations or family units sharing a single household.

fields.title: Kitchen Role
fields.label: Kitchen Role
fields.subtitle: Primary identity in meal preparation responsibilities
fields.caption: Overwhelmingly primary caregivers (221/232, 95%) — appliances are tools for fulfilling care duties, not optional hobbies.
fields.how_to_read: A near-unanimous 'primary_caregiver' signals meal prep is a non-negotiable responsibility, not a choice.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from how the respondent described their relationship to cooking responsibilities.

legend.label: Primary Caregiver
legend.description: Meal preparation is a core caregiving duty, not a discretionary activity.

legend.label: Shared Responsibility
legend.description: Cooking duties are distributed among household members.

legend.label: Working Professional
legend.description: Approaches cooking as a time-constrained necessity between work demands.

legend.label: Business Cook
legend.description: Prepares food commercially — appliance needs are revenue-driven.

fields.title: Cook Self-Image
fields.label: Cook Self-Image
fields.subtitle: How the respondent perceives their own cooking competence
fields.caption: Nearly universal competence (229/232, 99%) — messaging should avoid beginner framing and respect established skills.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'competent' bar signals confidence in cooking abilities, not insecurity needing remediation.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from self-descriptions of cooking skills and kitchen confidence.

legend.label: Competent
legend.description: Views self as skilled and capable in meal preparation.

legend.label: Mixed
legend.description: Has areas of confidence and insecurity in cooking abilities.

legend.label: Struggling
legend.description: Lacks confidence in cooking skills and seeks support.

legend.label: Efficient
legend.description: Prioritizes speed/systemization over culinary artistry.

fields.title: Appliance as Identity
fields.label: Appliance as Identity
fields.subtitle: Degree to which appliances reflect personal identity
fields.caption: Mostly medium (225/232, 97%) — appliances are practical tools, not strong identity markers or status symbols.
fields.how_to_read: A central 'medium' tendency signals functional rather than expressive appliance relationships.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from how the respondent described the role of appliances in self-presentation.

legend.label: Medium
legend.description: Appliance choices reflect practical needs more than personal identity.

legend.label: High
legend.description: Views appliances as extensions of personal style or values.

legend.label: Low
legend.description: Treats appliances as purely utilitarian with no identity component.

sections.title: Voice of the Respondent — Respondent Profiles

fields.title: Switching Consideration
fields.label: Switching Consideration
fields.subtitle: Whether the respondent is actively considering switching brands
fields.caption: Only 13/233 (6%) are considering switching — most are locked into current brands, making share-stealing difficult without breakthrough innovation.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'False' signals strong brand inertia where minor improvements won't drive switching.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from expressions of openness to alternative brands.

legend.label: False
legend.description: Not actively considering switching appliance brands.

legend.label: True
legend.description: Open to or actively evaluating alternative appliance brands.

fields.title: Relationship Stage
fields.label: Relationship Stage
fields.subtitle: Current phase in the brand-appliance ownership lifecycle
fields.caption: Most are settled/satisfied (169/233, 73%) — the market is mature with few new adopters or dissatisfied users to recruit.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'settled_satisfied' signals contentment that requires significant pain points to disrupt.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from descriptions of satisfaction and future purchase intent.

legend.label: Settled Satisfied
legend.description: Content with current appliance and not seeking alternatives.

legend.label: Strained
legend.description: Experiencing appliance frustrations but hasn't yet decided to replace.

legend.label: Honeymoon
legend.description: Recently purchased and still in enthusiastic early use phase.

legend.label: At Risk
legend.description: Actively dissatisfied and likely to switch brands soon.

legend.label: Resigned Acceptance
legend.description: Keeps appliance despite dissatisfaction due to lack of better options.

fields.title: Loyalty Depth
fields.label: Loyalty Depth
fields.subtitle: Nature of attachment to current appliance brands
fields.caption: Overwhelmingly functional loyalty (218/232, 94%) — few feel emotional connections, leaving brands vulnerable to better-performing alternatives.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'functional' signals rational rather than emotional bonds that features/performance could disrupt.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from how the respondent described their reasons for sticking with current brands.

legend.label: Functional
legend.description: Stays with brand for practical performance reasons, not emotional attachment.

legend.label: Emotional
legend.description: Feels genuine affection or identity alignment with the brand.

legend.label: Surface
legend.description: No particular loyalty — would switch for minor conveniences.

fields.title: Advocacy Likelihood
fields.label: Advocacy Likelihood
fields.subtitle: Probability the respondent would recommend their current appliance brand
fields.caption: Strong advocacy intent (201/232, 87%) — most users are willing brand promoters if given opportunities to share experiences.
fields.how_to_read: A dominant 'will_recommend' signals a receptive base for referral programs or testimonial campaigns.
fields.calc_note: AI-classified from expressions of willingness to recommend the brand to others.

legend.label: Will Recommend
legend.description: Likely to proactively recommend the brand to friends/family.

legend.label: Might Recommend
legend.description: Would answer if asked but won't initiate recommendations.

fields.title: NPS Signal
fields.label: NPS Signal
fields.subtitle: Net Promoter Score classification based on advocacy behavior
fields.caption: Promoters dominate (132/233, 57%) but passives (64/233, 27%) represent untapped potential — improving their experience could significantly boost NPS.
fields.how_to_read: The gap between promoters and passives shows room to elevate satisfied-but-not-enthusiastic users.
fields.calc_note: Calculated from advocacy likelihood and satisfaction expressions in transcript.

legend.label: Promoter
legend.description: Enthusiastic advocate likely to drive positive word-of-mouth.

legend.label: Passive
legend.description: Satisfied but unenthusiastic — won't actively promote the brand.

legend.label: Detractor
legend.description: Unhappy user likely to share negative experiences.

legend.label: Unclear
legend.description: Insufficient evidence to classify advocacy tendency.

sections.title: Emotional Resolution

sections.calc_note: AI-classified from emotional tone when describing appliance experiences.

sections.title: Price Sensitivity

sections.caption: Most are medium sensitivity (171/194, 88%) — willing to pay for quality but need clear value justification over budget options.
sections.how_to_read: A central 'medium' tendency signals balanced value-seeking rather than pure price minimization.
sections.calc_note: AI-classified from descriptions of purchase decision criteria and tradeoffs.
